title: API Management Authentication and Security
description: Secure your APIs in APIM using OAuth 2.0, JWT validation, mutual certificates, and subscription keys.

data.text: APIM provides multiple layers of security. At the gateway level, you can require subscription keys or mutual TLS. At the API level, you can validate JWTs issued by Entra ID or another identity provider.

data.title: APIM Security Options
items: OAuth 2.0 — validate JWT tokens from Entra ID
Mutual TLS — require clients to present a certificate
IP filtering — allow or deny specific IP ranges

data.title: Require Subscription Key and Validate JWT
data.content: Combine subscription key enforcement with JWT validation in a policy.
data.code:
<policies>
  <inbound>
    <base />
    <check-header name="Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key"
      failed-check-httpcode="401"
      failed-check-error-message="Missing subscription key" />
    <validate-jwt header-name="Authorization"
      failed-validation-httpcode="401">
      <openid-config url="https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration" />
      <required-claims>
        <claim name="roles" match="any">
          <value>API.Access</value>
        </claim>
      </required-claims>
    </validate-jwt>
  </inbound>
</policies>

data.title: Call an APIM API with a Subscription Key
data.content: Include the subscription key in a request to APIM.

data.title: Defense in Depth
data.text: Use multiple security layers. Subscription keys prevent casual abuse; JWT validation ensures only authorized users call your APIs. Neither is sufficient alone.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Subscription keys are the simplest way to secure APIM APIs.
JWT validation ties API access to Entra ID identities.
Mutual TLS is the strongest option for machine-to-machine communication.
data.takeaway: Layer your security: subscription key + JWT + IP filtering for sensitive APIs.
